people.name: Natalie Kolodij
sources: Natalie Kolodij official biography and teaching role
Real estate filing, strategy, implementation and directory
people.profile: Kolodij Tax & Consulting identifies Natalie Kolodij as an enrolled agent, real estate tax educator and founder of the Certified Real Estate Tax Strategist credential.
people.offering: The firm describes a full-service package with a custom plan, quarterly calls, implementation and year-end tax filing. It also points to a separate directory of professionals trained in real estate taxation.
people.scenario: You own rentals and need depreciation records, quarterly decisions and tax returns coordinated. Compare the direct firm engagement with a directory referral and assign property-level implementation and filing.
questions: Is the contract with Kolodij Tax or a separately listed strategist?
Which properties, entities and returns are included?
Who implements recommendations and checks depreciation records?
What quarterly access, availability and full fees apply?
people.boundary: The reviewed firm page includes implementation and filing and advertises limited openings. Confirm current availability. A strategist-directory introduction does not guarantee Natalie personally performs the work or that all firms share one scope.
people.fee: The reviewed official pages do not publish one fixed fee for every real estate engagement. Request the current quote for the property count, entities, quarterly work and return list.

people.name: Steven Jarvis
sources: Steven Jarvis official public education profile
people.profile: Retirement Tax Services describes Steven Jarvis’s public work through podcasts, articles and practical tax education for financial advisors.
people.offering: The reviewed homepage markets advisor memberships with training, community and CPA tax-return reviews; higher-tier services include office hours and a strategy call. Compare those advisor-facing benefits with a separately agreed taxpayer service.
people.scenario: Your financial advisor follows the RTS podcast and wants help evaluating a client tax return. Establish who contracts for the review, who may rely on it and who handles client advice, implementation and filing.
questions: Is the buyer an advisor or a taxpayer?
What return reviews and office-hour access are included?
Who contracts for personal advice and return preparation?
Who implements recommendations and what renewals apply?
people.boundary: Membership support for an advisor is not automatically a direct engagement with the advisor’s client. The reviewed site is not education only: its tiers include CPA return-review support. Confirm current taxpayer-service availability separately.
people.fee: The reviewed RTS homepage lists Essentials at $297/month and Premiere at $597/month. These are advisor membership prices, not universal private taxpayer planning or tax-preparation quotes. Confirm current terms and scope.

people.name: David McKnight
people.brand: Power of Zero / David McKnight & Company
sources: David McKnight official author and team biography
Advisor marketing program and consumer advisor route
people.profile: Power of Zero identifies David McKnight as its president and author of retirement-oriented books including The Power of Zero and Tax-Free Income for Life.
people.offering: The public platform distinguishes a program for financial advisors from a route for consumers seeking a Power of Zero advisor. Compare books and advisor education with the specific professional services and products offered under a separate agreement.
people.scenario: You read about tax-free retirement and want to coordinate business income with retirement decisions. Ask for a documented analysis of your actual circumstances and separate tax advice from investment or insurance product decisions.
questions: Am I purchasing education or engaging a specific advisor?
Who reviews my tax records and prepares projections?
Which advisory, investment or insurance fees and compensation apply?
Who coordinates implementation, custody and tax filing?
people.boundary: A branded planning approach and advisor introduction do not establish personal access to David or a guaranteed tax-free outcome. AE advisory fees do not cover investment management, custody or insurance products; compare each proposal’s actual scope.
people.fee: The reviewed homepage and team biography do not establish a single private-client fee. Request the actual advisor’s written fee schedule and any product compensation separately from book or training costs.

people.name: Hannah Smolinski
sources: Fractional CFO scope, pricing and existing tax-team coordination
people.profile: Clara CFO Group identifies Hannah Smolinski as a CPA, founder and CEO. Its public platform includes educational resources, a podcast and YouTube links.
people.offering: The firm describes fractional CFO work including forecasting, budgeting, reporting, KPI tracking, finance leadership and implementation support. Its FAQ says it works alongside existing accountants, bookkeepers and tax preparers.
people.scenario: You learned from a finance video and now need cash-flow forecasts and a finance leader. Compare CFO ownership and meeting cadence with a tax plan; the same business may need both services.
questions: Who owns forecasting, budgeting and finance-team leadership?
How does the CFO coordinate with my tax preparer?
Which system implementation and transaction support are included?
What monthly scope, reporting and additional fees apply?
people.boundary: The FAQ describes CFO services for businesses generally in the $2M–$20M revenue range and coordination with existing tax professionals. Confirm fit and current scope; a CFO engagement should not be treated as an automatic replacement for tax preparation.
people.fee: The reviewed FAQ says most clients invest $3,500–$10,000 per month depending on CFO ownership and complexity. That recurring CFO range is not a like-for-like quote for AE’s defined tax advisory engagement.

people.name: Nayo Carter-Gray
sources: 1st Step Accounting founder and firm identity
Bookkeeping, preparation and proactive planning services
Customized flat-fee proposal and filing scope
people.profile: 1st Step Accounting identifies Nayo Carter-Gray as its founder. Her public tax and accounting education is connected to a virtual business-service practice.
people.offering: The firm describes bookkeeping, bookkeeping review, tax preparation, planning and financial guidance. The pricing page says services are selected and scoped in a customized flat-fee proposal.
people.scenario: You want a virtual team to connect monthly books, business returns and projections. Compare the actual service selections and ask which tasks are one-time versus ongoing.
questions: Which bookkeeping, planning and returns are selected?
Is the bookkeeping review separately priced?
Who handles cleanup, projections and implementation?
What deposit, ongoing support and scope-change terms apply?
people.boundary: The pricing page says some engagements include preparation and others focus on different services. Confirm your specific return list. A public course, discovery call or illustrative sample proposal is not a complete client engagement.
people.fee: The reviewed pricing page describes customized flat fees quoted before work, with a deposit and agreed payment schedule. Its sample is illustrative and contains no universal dollar quote; request the current proposal for the services you select.

pairs: Compare real estate tax proposals using the same properties, entities, depreciation records, implementation assignments, quarterly review schedule and year-end returns. Separate a direct engagement from a trained-professional directory introduction.
Compare advisor-facing education and CPA review support with IRA education and advisor introductions. Establish the buyer, return-review limits and separate taxpayer engagement before comparing fees.
Compare retirement education, professional training and advisor introductions by actual deliverables. Identify the engaged advisor and any investment, insurance, tax or filing responsibilities.
Compare fractional CFO ownership with accounting, compliance and advisory services under the actual firm contract. Assign forecasts, monthly books, payroll and tax filings separately.

Compare customized virtual accounting proposals and their preparation responsibilities. 1st Step describes selected preparation services; Pai’s reviewed page uses a separate Tax CPA for income tax filings.
selection: Five absent identities confirmed against 39-creator inventory and compare routes. Official education and service sources; no measured search-demand ranking.
